newsitem.title: FRANCE: BNP H1 prompts full-year upgrades.
newsitem.headline: BNP H1 prompts full-year upgrades.

text.p: A surprise surge in first-half profits at Banque Nationale de Paris and positive sentiment prompted upgrades of full-year profit forecasts by several financial analysts.
"I'm raising, it was a nice surprise," said EIFB analyst Sami Gotrane. "It's pretty good for bank generally," he said.
The bank was set to operate at a much healthier level of around 7.0 percent return on equity after some time stuck at only half that level, he said after a post-results meeting.
He was raising his full-year forecast for net attributable profit to 3.2 billion francs from under three billion.
Another French brokerage said it was raising its profit forecast to 3.2 from 3.0 billion francs.

Analyst Jim Hyde at Williams de Broe said he was raising his forecast to 3.05 billion from 2.5 billion for 1996 and looking for 3.435 billion in 1997 after results which hinted at a "sustained recovery".

BNP earlier reported a first-half net attributable profit up 80 percent at 1.735 billion francs and net banking income up for the first time in two years at 19.223 billion from 18.334 billion. The stock was 2.11 percent up at 193.5 francs at 1444 GMT after a day high of 197.4 with over 1.5 million shares traded.

A source at Morgan Stanley said the investment bank had put BNP on its list of "Fresh Money Buys", a list of at most 10 European stocks seen as having strong potential. Morgan Stanley was keepinga "strong buy" on BNP stock, the source said.
